events.summary:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues.

* WHERE...Southern Mineral County in south central Colorado...

* WHEN...Until 100 PM MDT.

* IMPACTS...Flooding of rivers, creeks, streams, and other low-lying
and flood-prone locations is imminent or occurring. Numerous roads,
including Highway 160, remain closed due to flooding.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 1041 AM MDT, Doppler radar indicated heavy rain. Flooding is
already occurring in the warned area. Between 2 and 4 inches of
rain have fallen over the previous 48 hours.
- Flooding impacts will continue, but no additional rainfall is
expected.
- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
Wolf Creek Pass.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

* WHERE...San Juan River at Shiprock.

* WHEN...Until Sunday afternoon.

just after midnight tonight. It will then fall below flood stage
early Sunday morning.
- Flood stage is 15.5 feet.

...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in New
Mexico...

Animas River At Farmington affecting San Juan County.

* WHAT...Minor flooding is forecast.

* WHERE...Animas River at Farmington.

* WHEN...Until late Saturday night.

* IMPACTS...At 12.0 feet, The riverwalk area in Farmington is flooded
and should be avoided. Water levels have not been this high since
the flood of 1927.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 4:45 AM MDT Friday the stage was 9.2 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 9.0 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to rise above flood stage late
this morning to a crest of 11.3 feet late this evening. It will
then fall below flood stage early tomorrow afternoon.
- Flood stage is 10.0 feet.
- Flood History...This crest compares to a previous crest of 11.0
feet on 05/14/1941.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

events.source_name: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.summary:
...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in New
Mexico...

Animas River Near Cedar Hill affecting San Juan County.

* WHAT...Minor flooding is forecast. This approaches the flood of
record.

* WHERE...Animas River near Cedar Hill.

* WHEN...Until Saturday afternoon.

* IMPACTS...At 10.5 feet, Flood waters will inundate low spots along
the river and property damage may become more widespread if further
rises occur. Portions of the riverwalk in Farmington will soon be
flooded and impassable. At 11.5 feet, The river would be near an
all time high. Areas along the river that never before experienced
flooding will likely be inundated as water levels continue to rise.
At 9.5 feet, Minor overbank flooding of low spots along the river
from the New Mexico-Colorado border down to the riverwalk in
Farmington can be expected.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 10:00 AM MDT Friday the stage was 10.2 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 9.5 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to rise to a crest of 11.3 feet
late this afternoon. It will then fall below flood stage just
after midnight tonight.
- Flood stage is 10.5 feet.
- Flood History...This crest compares to a previous crest of 11.3
feet on 09/06/1970.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

events.title: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.region: Northern Foot Hills; Butte County Area; Northern Campbell; Southern Campbell; Crook County Plains; Weston County Plains; Wyoming Black Hills
events.source_name: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.summary:
...RED FLAG WARNING REMAINS IN EFFECT UNTIL 11 PM MDT THIS EVENING
DUE TO GUSTY WINDS AND LOW RELATIVE HUMIDITY FOR NORTHERN FOOT HILLS,
BUTTE COUNTY AREA, NORTHERN CAMPBELL, SOUTHERN CAMPBELL, CROOK COUNTY
PLAINS, WESTON COUNTY PLAINS, AND WYOMING BLACK HILLS...

.Warm temperatures, humidities as low as 13%, and southwest winds
gusting to 50 mph ahead of an approaching cold front will create
widespread critical fire weather conditions Friday afternoon through
Friday evening. Southwest winds increase over northeastern Wyoming
after 10 am Friday morning with sustained winds of 25 to 35 mph and
gusts of 40 to 50 mph through the afternoon. Winds will shift to the
northwest after midnight as the front moves through. While some
showers may accompany the front, not expecting any widespread wetting
rains.

* AFFECTED AREA...Fire Weather Zones 314, 315, 316, 317, 318, 323,
and 327.

* TIMING...Until 11 PM MDT this evening.

* WINDS...Southwest winds 25 to 35 mph with gusts up to 50 mph.

* RELATIVE HUMIDITY...As low as 13 percent.

* IMPACTS...Any fires that develop will spread rapidly. Outdoor
burning is not recommended.
